kind: readonly design review for a source-host CSR diagnostic

baseline.reported_observation: 113 MMIO events, six writes; reset/run deasserted and both observed PU/PD pairs remained zero. The measured 100us run interval is timed-only, not calibration success or failure.
baseline.frozen_state: MicroReset=1 (stalled), MuxSel=0, UcclkHclkEnables=3, MemResetL=2, ZCalRate=9 before and after, PclkDivRatio=0x1111. Controller remains held and DFI initialization is not triggered.

address_and_provenance.direct_interface_evidence: pmu_clock.c pmu_phy_clk_phase_toggle_pulse, lines 371-390, writes p[32]=0,1,0 after p[17]=0 and before restoring p[3]. dwc_ddrphy_pmu_regs.h line370 defines the halfword base as 0x90040600. Independently named surrounding CSRs identify p[16]/p[17] as ZCal reset/run; the helper's clock-phase comment does not establish register semantics.
address_and_provenance.independent_host_evidence: SiMa PUB220 and NXP PUB230 ordinary CSR SAVE address lists both include logical20320. Their host loops read this CSR through the APB path. See zcal-companion-microreset-review.json for exact commits, blobs and source lines.
address_and_provenance.allowed_use: Non-program host CSR address and direct access-order facts only. No vendor binary, ARC execution, PMU IMEM, PIE program or opaque executable descriptor is imported.
address_and_provenance.unknown: The complete bitfield definition and electrical effect of20320 remain unknown. Result latch is only a hypothesis. Existing zero readback alone did not justify a write; the separately documented public direct-write precedent is the additional basis for this bounded experiment.

recommended_isolation.reference: Reproduce the already tested Rate113 six-write sequence and measured waits, adding only the20320 pulse between Run=0 and successful-path Rate=9 restoration.
sequence: Validate the exact current source-held controller, PHY ownership, clock and analog baseline; read20320=0 and2030d=0 before any write.
ZCalReset=1; measured reset interval and readback.
Require exact Reset=0 and Run=0; capture PU/PD as raw observations before the new pulse.
Write20320 halfword0, then1, then0, with exact readback after each write. Keep all other bits zero because the complete initial halfword must have been zero.
Capture PU/PD raw observations after the pulse, while Rate remains0x19.
Only after all prior steps succeed, restore ZCalRate=9 with exact readback; require Reset=0, Run=0 and20320=0, capture PU/PD once more, and verify the complete frozen context.
recommended_isolation.why_rate19: Relative to the nearest hardware baseline,20320 is the only added mutation. Leaving Rate at9 would also change the Rate113 condition and would need a different reference experiment.
not_included: No2030d/host61a pulse: it is a separate untested factor.
No PLL, clock gate, MicroReset, MemResetL, voltage, range or override changes.
No MR commands, DFI completion forcing, instruction memory, DRAM data or storage access.

stop_and_interpretation.failure: Any guard, timer, UART, access or readback failure stops immediately. Do not pulse remaining values, restore Rate or issue speculative cleanup after failure. A failed write may already have changed hardware.
stop_and_interpretation.self_clearing_unknown: No evidence establishes whether writing1 must persist. A readback other than1 is an observed mismatch and stops this exact contract; do not silently classify it as a successful self-clearing strobe.
stop_and_interpretation.timing_limit: APB writes, barriers, readbacks and UART logging space the edges. No minimum or maximum20320 pulse width is established. A negative result does not exclude a timing-sensitive role.
stop_and_interpretation.zero_result: Unchanged PU/PD zero remains ambiguous; this does not prove calibration failure.
stop_and_interpretation.changed_result: Changed PU/PD would establish a correlation with this controlled host operation, not DDR training, valid impedance, DRAM access or Armbian boot.
stop_and_interpretation.success_label: Timed pulse completed and observed only; never calpass or trained.
